name: James Rennell Rodd
bio: Poet and diplomat, later British Ambassador to Italy (1908-19) and first Lord Rennell of Rodd. A friend of Wilde at Oxford, where he won the Newdigate Prize in 1880, two years after Wilde. Wilde wrote the 'envoi' to his Rose Leaf and Apple Leaf (1882) and published, as its dedication, an inscription Rodd had written privately in Wilde's own copy — 'TO OSCAR WILDE— HEART'S BROTHER' — which Rodd found much more effusive than he had intended, and which helped end the friendship.
bio_note: Added 2026-08-05, per Lovelle, as a NODE WITH NO CONNECTION: he is documented in Wilde's circle but nothing read supports a romantic or sexual edge, and Lovelle asked for him on the map without one. Dates 1858-1941 and the biography are from the editors' note 4 at Complete Letters printed 102, folio confirmed on the rendered page image. ONLY ONE LETTER to Rodd survives in the volume, headed 'To Rennell Rodd' at printed 102-103 (the whole of the correspondence, checked by extracting every letter heading in the OCR mirror). Its affection amounts to the salutation 'Dear Rennell' and the closing 'Come back very soon'; it is a letter of congratulation on Rodd's Second in Greats, signed 'Truly yours'. WHY NO EDGE: the warmest surviving item is the 'Heart's Brother' inscription, which is Rodd's phrase and not Wilde's, and which Rodd objected to seeing in print. It sits in the same register the Complete Letters sweep ruled 'warm, and not desire' for Sherard's dedication. Ellmann's one suggestive line - that the two travelled under false names 'presumably to keep Rodd's friends from suspecting that their intimacy was so constant' (repo PDF 189) - is flagged by Ellmann himself as a presumption, and the editors' own note at printed 101 says the travelling companion was 'almost certainly Rennell Rodd', which is a second hedge on top of the first.

context_engagements.period: Oxford friendship from the late 1870s; the correspondence survives only for 1880
context_engagements.note: Recorded as a context engagement rather than a connection: documented friendship, no romantic or sexual claim. The single surviving letter is quoted in full below for its affectionate register, which is the whole of what the correspondence offers.

sources.quote: Dear Rennell, My best congratulations. Greats is the only fine school at Oxford, the only sphere of thought where one can be, simultaneously, brilliant and unreasonable, speculative and well-informed, creative as well as critical, and write with all the passion of youth about the truths which belong to the august serenity of old age. I wish you had got a First, that my compeers should not all be sluggish and syllogistic Scotchmen; still, a Second is perhaps for a man of culture a sweeter atmosphere than the chilly Caucasus of an atheistical First. Come back very soon. Truly yours
sources.context: Wilde to Rennell Rodd, circa 4 December 1880, Keats House (MS Private) - the only letter to Rodd in the volume, congratulating him on his Second in Greats, announced in The Times on 4 December 1880.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: The entire surviving correspondence, and the extent of the affection in it: 'Dear Rennell' and 'Come back very soon'.
sources.provenance: Repo PDF pages 127-128; printed folios 102 and 103 both confirmed on the rendered page images, read 2026-08-05. The letter runs across the page break and is transcribed whole.
